title: Cartesian-edge transitivity for two inner fibrations
statement: Use quasicategories and simplicial maps of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations and cartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A,D,B$ be quasicategories in a fixed universe, let $a:A\to D$ and $b:D\to B$ be inner fibrations, and let $h:u\to v$ be an edge of $A$. Suppose $a(h)$ is $b$-cartesian. Then $h$ is $a$-cartesian if and only if it is $(b\circ a)$-cartesian.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.6 (Transitivity), assertion (1), restricted to quasicategories. Statement and full mapping-space/pasting proof read online 2026-10-17. This is a Kerodon identifier, not a Stacks tag; no Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion. Archive WANTED.

proof.text: Put $r=b\circ a$. This is an inner fibration: given an inner-horn lifting problem for $r$, first apply $a$ to its upper horn and fill over its given base simplex using the inner fibration $b$. This gives a simplex in $D$ with the prescribed $a$-image of the horn. Lift this simplex with the original horn using $a$. The resulting simplex in $A$ solves the original problem. Thus the cartesian mapping-space criterion applies to $a$, $b$ and $r$, with exactly the quasicategory hypotheses in the statement.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.6 (1), proof: mapping-space diagram, bottom square, transitivity and varying the test object. Online source, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $z\in A$. Write $M_C(x,y)=\operatorname{Map}_C(x,y)$ in the specified right-pinched convention. These are Kan complexes by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Form the stacked diagram $$\begin{array}{ccc}M_A(z,u)&\xrightarrow{h\circ-}&M_A(z,v)\\ \downarrow a_*&&\downarrow a_*\\ M_D(az,au)&\xrightarrow{a(h)\circ-}&M_D(az,av)\\ \downarrow b_*&&\downarrow b_*\\ M_B(rz,ru)&\xrightarrow{r(h)\circ-}&M_B(rz,rv).\end{array}$$ The postcomposition maps and their coherent commutation with $a_*,b_*$ are supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], whose action in the second variable is canonical postcomposition. Use those naturality squares, and take their concatenated commutation homotopy for the outer rectangle. The vertical composite is $r_*$: in degree $n$ both composites send a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to A$ to $b\circ a\circ\sigma$. Composing the coherent natural transformations for $a_*$ and $b_*$ therefore supplies the functor-induced square for $r$ with this concatenated homotopy. In particular this is a coherent diagram of spaces, not just a diagram of component sets.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.6 (1), proof: mapping-space diagram, bottom square, transitivity and varying the test object. Online source, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The hypothesis says that $a(h):a(u)\to a(v)$ is $b$-cartesian. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] to $p=b$, $s=a(h)$ and the test vertex $a(z)\in D$. It says exactly that the lower square in step 2 is a homotopy pullback. This uses no lifting-existence hypothesis for any other edge of $D$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.6 (1), proof: mapping-space diagram, bottom square, transitivity and varying the test object. Online source, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] to the diagram of step 2 read with its two coordinates interchanged: its top row is $M_A(z,u)\to M_D(az,au)\to M_B(rz,ru)$ and its bottom row is $M_A(z,v)\to M_D(az,av)\to M_B(rz,rv)$. The right square is the lower square of step 2 and is a homotopy pullback by step 3. The cited pasting theorem, including its specified-homotopy clause, gives that the left square is a homotopy pullback if and only if the outer rectangle is. In the original orientation these are precisely the upper square and outer rectangle of step 2; the latter uses the concatenated homotopy specified there.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.2.6 (1), proof: mapping-space diagram, bottom square, transitivity and varying the test object. Online source, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The equivalence of step 4 holds for every vertex $z\in A$. Hence the upper squares are homotopy pullbacks for all such $z$ if and only if the outer rectangles are. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] first to $(a,h)$ and then to $(r,h)$, using the inner-fibration verification in step 1. These two universally quantified conditions are respectively that $h$ is $a$-cartesian and that $h$ is $r$-cartesian. This proves both directions of the asserted equivalence.

Its proof (bottom square by 5.1.2.1, pasting by 3.4.1.11, then vary the test object) is what steps 3-5 follow. Small cases I tested: nerves of ordinary categories (where it is the classical strongly-cartesian cancellation), B a point (equivalences), and a=id or b=id (both trivially true). Empty mapping spaces are allowed by every cited node. Step 1 (a composite of inner fibrations is inner) really is elementary. One coherence point I checked and accept: the criterion's proof models the postcomposition square by a strict slice roof, while the item uses the Hom-bifunctor naturality squares. Both are the canonical postcomposition square and the item treats them the same way in steps 3 and 5, so this does not use a proof in place of a statement.
